page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine in the N1 family based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz, mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 15.0 GB of memory (3.75 GB per vCPU) and an L3 cache of 45 MB. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES encryption, FMA, and BMI2 instructions, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. It includes no bundled GPUs or local NVMe storage, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the server's CPU and memory performance primarily in the lower tiers across synthetic evaluations. In stress-ng, single-core and multi-core CPU scores register at 1107.78 and 2904.55 respectively, placing in the bottom 25%. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 25.29 GB/sec, and write bandwidth reaches 21.61 GB/sec. Application-specific benchmarks show 2.68 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, a PassMark database score of 1230.38, and a static web serving throughput of 2.46 GB/sec. Small 135M model LLM text generation performs at 59.16 tokens/sec. With lower relative raw compute throughput, this instance delivers a balanced configuration for light-to-moderate general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, and lightweight background task processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-4 is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon processor at 2.3 GHz, split across 2 physical cores, and paired with 15.0 GB of memory. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the server includes 45 MB of L3 cache, AVX vector extensions, and AES acceleration, but lacks local SSD storage and integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show single-core and multi-core CPU performance in the bottom 25% with stress-ng scores of 1107.78 and 2904.55. Memory bandwidth reads max out at 25.29 GB/sec for large blocks, while static web serving throughput reaches 2.46 GB/sec and Redis SET operations process 2.68 million requests per second. Given its resource profile and baseline processing capabilities, the instance is suited for routine general-purpose tasks, low-traffic web applications, and basic database operations that do not require intense memory bandwidth or heavy CPU execution.
